script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for October 30. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Your ancestors walked 10 miles daily, lifted heavy things, ran from predators.  Your body expects movement.  When you don't move, it interprets stillness as illness and starts shutting down.

Muscles grow when challenged. Bones strengthen under load. Hearts improve with cardio demands. Your body builds capacity for what you ask it to do—and removes capacity for what you don't. Exercise isn't just physical—it improves mood, reduces anxiety, sharpens thinking.  Your brain grows new neurons during movement.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Bodies are built to move.  Use your capacity or lose it.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Movement Audit - How Much Do You Move?.

Here's your activity: How much do you move in a typical day? Walking, exercise, physical activity? Is it enough to maintain the capacity you want? What one addition would improve your movement pattern? This helps you assess current movement and plan improvements.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about why moving matters can be applied to movement audit - how much do you move?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
